steps.title: Three special moves
steps.body: Castling, en passant, and promotion each follow their own rule.

steps.title: Castling
steps.body: The king moves two squares toward a rook, and the rook jumps over it. Neither piece may have moved before, the king cannot pass through an attacked square, and it cannot castle out of check.

steps.title: En passant
steps.body: When a pawn jumps two squares past an enemy pawn that could have captured it, the enemy may capture it en passant on the very next move.

steps.title: Promotion
steps.body: Push the pawn on a7 to the last rank and promote it.
steps.hint: A pawn that reaches the last rank becomes any piece except a king or pawn. A queen is the usual choice.
steps.success: Promotion done. A queen is usually the best choice, but any of the four is legal.

steps.question: Can a king castle after it has moved?
steps.explanation: Once the king moves, castling is no longer allowed.
